title: The wall clock firing emits no feed event
description:
Found by tick rj0 (run epic-9pd, attempt 16), which went looking for it after being split out of emk and reported that it had been dropped.

emk asked for three things. rj0 took the stop (1) and the snapshot interaction (3). Item 2 — the wall clock firing is a FEED event and appears in ticfac status, not only an observation line in the attempt's own state — landed in no open tick. The operator split emk and lost it; the worker checked rather than assuming, which is why it is here.

Still wanted, and now cheaper: with rj0 the stop lands within a poll of the bound, so the attempt settles and the collected verdict says so. But at the moment the bound fires the feed says nothing, and the feed is what a watcher reads.

Note the constraint that made this awkward in the first place: the observation KIND enum in contracts/job-protocol.json is closed, so a typed wall-stop observation across the executor seam would be a pinned-bundle change. The feed line itself is reconciler-side and needs no contract change — the question is how the reconciler learns the bound fired without matching prose.

7zs is a different thing: that is the earlier no-progress signal, before the bound.

2026-09-18 05:59 - ticfac run epic-9pd: attempt 27 reported a finding drafted for triage — proposed-tick "Tick q1e's description said the feed-line half 'landed in no open tick', but it had landed with emk before q1e was filed" (key 674edf31a7bbb7f86631ccb7588c04e5dd3c960897a1f506a2a60a99f74ceff6, severity low, for this repository). Triage with `ticfac finding 9pd 674edf31a7bbb7f86631ccb7588c04e5dd3c960897a1f506a2a60a99f74ceff6 --promote-as <tick> --by "<who>"`, `--discard --by "<who>"`, or — when it was repaired inside this epic — `--fixed-as <commit> --by "<who>"`; the tick cannot close while it is untriaged.
2026-09-18 06:10 - Correction to this tick's own description, from the attempt that worked it.

The description said the feed-line half had 'landed in no open tick'. That was wrong when it was written: 1a7f811, merged via tick-emk/attempt-15 BEFORE q1e was filed, already implements the wall_clock_fired feed line, its once-per-tick guard and its marker-arithmetic derivation. The worker read the record, could not reconcile it with the code, and spent its time re-verifying a half that was already present and tested rather than trusting the record.

The error was the orchestrator's, in splitting emk: a tick split out of another must say what its sibling already landed, or the next worker pays to rediscover it. No code change follows from this - the half is there.
2026-09-18 06:21 - ticfac run epic-9pd: attempt 27 merged into epic/9pd as 79501029bb8a; the integrated gate (go) passed.
acceptance_criteria: The run writes a feed line when an attempt's wall clock fires, and ticfac status reports it for an in-flight attempt; neither is derived by matching observation prose
